parsed.rationale: The two computed properties `StreamingService.name` (package `Metadata`, `Shared/Metadata/Sources/Metadata/StreamingService.swift:20`) and `MusicServiceIdentifier.displayName` (package `MusicShareKit`, `Shared/MusicShareKit/Sources/MusicShareKit/Models/MusicTrack.swift:76`) live on structurally unrelated types in separate packages. Despite a high Jaccard similarity of 0.875, `name` on a `StreamingService` and `displayName` on a `MusicServiceIdentifier` represent distinct domain concepts — one describes a streaming service entity, the other a music-service identifier on a track model. Both records carry all context flags false, so no restraint marker applies, but the coincidence is purely structural: a short string-returning computed property is one of the most common shapes in any Swift codebase, and there is no evidence of a shared upstream package that is already a dependency of both `Metadata` and `MusicShareKit` that would make extraction safe and meaningful. Merging them would couple unrelated domain models without a clear semantic contract.
